title: functional regression eval — the detect→fix→verify loop actually raises the score with no regressions
premise: Unlike the recall evals (does the skill help an LLM FIND issues), this is a FUNCTIONAL gate for the convex-doctor-fix loop: applying the skill's fixes to a real project must STRICTLY raise the react-convex-doctor score AND introduce zero new finding rule-classes. The analyzer's own re-run is the oracle.
target_project: react-convex-doctor's bundled examples/convex-nextjs (the official Convex Next.js starter), copied portably (no node_modules / .git). Baseline score 94/100, 5 convex findings in convex/myFunctions.ts.

two_parts.A_deterministic_gate: gate.sh applies golden/myFunctions.fixed.ts (the loop's AUTO fixes) to a temp copy and asserts after.score > before.score AND (after_rules - before_rules) is empty. Reproducible, ~3s, $0, CI-able. Catches regressions from a doctor version bump, an example change, or a bad golden fix.
two_parts.B_llm_loop: n=3 Sonnet 4.6 fixer agents, each on its own isolated copy, read the convex-doctor-fix + convex-best-practices skills, then run the loop themselves: detect (doctor --json) → apply the AUTO fixes (auth checks + public→internal refs) and LEAVE the PROPOSE-class sequential-ctx-run → verify (re-run). Each agent's output is then INDEPENDENTLY re-scanned by the harness (not trusting self-report) under the same assertion.

assertion: PASS iff doctor(after).score > doctor(before).score AND no finding rule-class present in `after` was absent in `before`. Applied to the golden fix (part A) and to each LLM agent's independently re-scanned output (part B).
